answer: Two names on one vent betray themselves in one sample: a merged plume holds one tracer ratio, never two. Each identity hangs one vent from one thread of key-fixed length: the length sets vent height, and height fixes how far its plume spreads before crossing the horizon plane for sampling. One honest agent threads one vent once and burns one tracer charge per epoch; a farm with 1,000 identities threads 1,000 vents and burns 1,000 charges. Auditors recompute the expected ratio from thread length and epoch beacon; a sample fitting no registered length or a plume stopping early voids the epoch.
